_comment: PARTIALLY VERIFIED - see `verification`. Every row below was cross-checked on 2026-09-19 against three independent published summaries of Nepal's national immunisation schedule, which agreed with each other. That found and corrected one real error (fIPV, see `corrections`). It is NOT a check against the official Ministry of Health and Population / Family Welfare Division publication, and it is not a clinical sign-off. Somebody with the official schedule must still confirm every row before a health worker acts on this, and schedules move - fIPV, the PCV booster and TCV have all changed in recent years. The app reads only `vaccines`; `version` is what the mock reports and what a future GET /rules could override.
source: Cross-checked against published secondary sources, 2026-09-19. Not the official Ministry publication.

verification.method: Three independent published summaries of the national schedule, compared row by row; all three agreed.
sources: WHO Nepal / secondary summaries via web search, 2026-09-19
corrections: fIPV was 6 and 14 weeks; corrected to 14 weeks and 9 months. All three sources agree on 14 weeks + 9 months, 2 doses, and Nepal moved to the 2-dose fractional schedule from the single 14-week full IPV dose introduced in 2014.
confirmedUnchanged: JE 12 months - nationwide in routine immunisation since July 2016, not endemic-districts-only
verification.structuralCheck: The sources state a fully immunised child needs 7 contacts: birth, 6, 10, 14 weeks, 9, 12, 15 months. The corrected schedule produces exactly those seven and no others.
knownGaps: HPV for adolescent girls (school grades 6-10, and out-of-school girls aged 10) is part of the national programme but is outside this module, which stops at five years.
Td for pregnant women is part of EPI and is handled separately in the ANC contact form, not here.
A JE vaccine supply shortage was reported in Nepal in 2025. That is a supply problem, not a schedule change, but a due date this app shows may not be a dose a health post can actually give.

vaccines.protectsEn: Diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B, Hib
vaccines.protectsNp: डिप्थेरिया, हुपिङ खोकी, धनुष्टंकार, हेपाटाइटिस बी, हिब

vaccines._note: 14 weeks and 9 months, NOT 6 and 14 weeks. Corrected 2026-09-19 - see `verification.corrections`. Two fractional intradermal doses replaced the single full IPV dose Nepal introduced at 14 weeks in 2014.
